what: Full re-read of the board's flash, compared against the stored capture
why: The modem stopped producing DTMF and the fault survived a power cycle, which raised the question of whether this session had written flash.
board: 20.16 MHz Courier V.Everything, ID_SDL v4.03d, supervisor 7.4.16, DSP 3.1.2
method: 2048 ATGLK2=<seg>:<off> page dumps covering 0x80000-0xfffff, 707 s, parsed and compared byte for byte
conclusion: Flash is byte-identical to the earlier capture. Nothing in this session wrote it.
why it could not have happened: The ATGLK2W primitive is `mov [bx], ax` with DS=0. BX is 16 bits, so it can only address 0x0000-0xffff - low RAM and the peripheral control block at 0xff00. Flash at 0x80000+ is not reachable by that command at all.
Flash programming needs an unlock/command sequence, which nothing sent here issues.
The probe kernels only did IN/OUT on named ports and wrote inside their own RAM region; emit_ram_writes.py refuses to emit anything touching ports 0x10/0x12/0x14.
NVRAM, the other non-volatile store: Not directly verified, but settings live in a serial EEPROM bit-banged on P1 with the strobe on port 0x10, and none of those was ever written. ATI4 on the cold board showed every S-register at its documented default, which is what intact NVRAM looks like.
so the DTMF fault is: not something this session wrote - it is pre-existing on this unit, or in the DSP tone path the supervisor drives at runtime
